llm.answer:
**Core Graphics – Apple Developer Documentation (PDF)** *The following points capture the main ideas that appear across the three pages of the uploaded PDF.* | Topic | Key Points | Source | |-------|------------|--------| | **Framework Overview** | • Core Graphics is built on Apple’s Quartz 2‑D engine.
• It delivers low‑level, lightweight 2‑D rendering with “unmatched output fidelity.”
• Core Graphics handles path‑based drawing, geometric transformations, color management, off‑screen rendering, patterns, gradients, shading, image data handling, image creation, image masking, and PDF creation, display, and parsing.
• On macOS it also exposes services for display‑hardware control, low‑level user‑input events, and the windowing system. | [Source 1] | | **Supported Platforms** | • iOS 2.0+, iPadOS 2.0+, Mac Catalyst 13.1+, macOS 10.8+, tvOS 9.0+, visionOS 1.0+, watchOS 2.0+. | [Source 1] | | **Core Data Types** | • **CGFloat** – basic floating‑point scalar.
• **CGPoint** – point in 2‑D space.
• **CGSize** – width/height pair.
• **CGRect** – rectangle defined by origin and size.
• **CGVector** – 2‑D vector.
• **CGAffineTransform** – 2‑D linear transform. | [Source 2] | | **Primary Classes** | • **CGContext** – Quartz 2‑D drawing environment.
• **CGImage** – bitmap image or image mask.
• **CGPath / CGMutablePath** – immutable/​mutable graphic paths.
• **CGLayer** – off‑screen context for reusable content.
• **CGColor / CGColorSpace** – color components and color‑space definitions.
• **CGFont** – glyph and layout information for text.
• **CGPDFDocument** – PDF document representation.
• **CGDataConsumer / CGDataProvider** – abstractions for writing/reading raw data buffers.
• **CGShading / CGGradient** – smooth color transitions for radial/axial fills.
• **CGFunction** – callback‑based function for shading.
• **CGPattern** – 2‑D pattern for drawing paths. | [Source 2] | | **PDF‑Specific Types** | • **CGPDFMarkedContentItem** – represents marked content in a PDF.
• **CGPDFStructureElement** – structural element in a PDF. | [Source 3] | | **Rendering & Buffering** | • **CGRenderingBufferProvider** – provides rendering buffers.
• **CGBitmapParameters** – bitmap configuration parameters. | [Source 3] | | **Enumerations & Constants** | • Various enums for bitmap layout, component types, color models, tone‑mapping, etc.
• Constants and functions for common graphics operations. | [Source 3] | | **Quartz Services** | • **QuartzDisplayServices** – direct access to macOS window server for display‑hardware configuration.
• **QuartzEventServices** – manage event taps (filters) for observing/altering low‑level user‑input streams.
• **QuartzWindowServices** – query information about windows managed by the macOS window server. | [Source 3] | | **Documentation Structure** | • The PDF is organized into sections: geometric data types, framework classes, PDF utilities, services, and low‑level APIs (structures, enumerations, constants, functions). | [Source 1] | **Bottom line:** The Core Graphics framework is a comprehensive, low‑level 2‑D graphics engine that powers drawing, image, and PDF work across all Apple platforms. It exposes a rich set of geometric primitives, rendering contexts, image and PDF handling classes, and system‑level services for display and event management. The documentation provides the full API surface, including data types, classes, enumerations, constants, and helper services, enabling developers to build high‑fidelity graphics applications.
